edges.description: TMAO, structurally similar to acetylcholine, inhibits the cardiac M2 muscarinic receptor.
M2R inhibition disrupts parasympathetic (vagal) cardiac control.
The high-TMAO state is associated with slower conduction velocity and APD80/wavelength shortening, which may lower the reentry threshold and feed electrical remodeling that sustains AF.

Chronic pressure load stretches the atrium, and that stretch drives the fibrotic remodelling that creates the reentrant substrate. Hypertension is the commonest condition in patients presenting with new atrial fibrillation.

Targets the oxidative stress node specifically rather than the generic substrate, because the cited work shows NOX2 inhibition normalising atrial action potential duration and abolishing obesity-driven ion channel remodelling, placing NOX2 on the causal path.
Apnoeic episodes produce repeated intrathoracic pressure swings, hypoxaemia and surges of autonomic tone, which is why this targets the autonomic node rather than the fibrotic substrate.
Smoking appears among the established risk factors in cohort modelling but without an identified atrial mechanism, so it is recorded as predisposing to the fibrotic substrate rather than driving it.

Alcohol shortens atrial refractoriness and slows conduction, and the association is dose-defined above roughly one standard drink per day, which is why this targets electrical rather than structural remodelling.

Excess thyroid hormone shortens the atrial action potential and raises automaticity, a reversible electrical effect: restoring euthyroidism often restores sinus rhythm, which distinguishes it from the structural risk factors here.
